extracted.intended_audience: performers, comedians, actors, clowns learning slapstick/physical comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for creating and performing slapstick/physical comedy, emphasizing visual clarity, precise timing, escalation, and performer commitment. Useful for actors, physical comedians, clowns, and directors working on visual-gag-based comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: exaggerated physical activity
rubrics_metrics.description: A style of humor involving exaggerated physical activity that exceeds the boundaries of normal physical comedy. May involve intentional violence and violence by mishap, often resulting from physical abuse and/or inept use of props.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the scope: slapstick is about exaggeration and physical mishap. When producing/evaluating, check whether the action intentionally exceeds everyday physical behavior and whether mishap or prop-ineptitude are used as sources of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical Comedy Range (forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Slapstick proper; Pratfalls; Mime; Clowning; Exaggerated facial expressions; Collisions; Cartoonish actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate subforms depending on the gag — e.g., pratfalls for falls, mime for silent visual gags, exaggerated facial expressions for close-ups. Selection of form should match the joke's visual needs and performer skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeating a gag can increase payoff as long as each iteration justifies itself (through escalation, variation, or timing). Beware of diminishing returns; repetition should build to a punchline or escalation rather than become stale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inversion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surprising the audience by subverting expectations enhances the comic effect. Plan setups that imply one outcome and execute the opposite for comedic reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telegraphing intent and then delaying execution increases comedic tension; balance is key so the telegraph gives the audience the cue without spoiling the gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure sequences so each beat increases consequences or absurdity. Escalation sustains interest and magnifies laughter when the final payoff arrives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing (micro-precision)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Micro-timing (subtle splits of seconds) determines whether a gag lands. Evaluate beats at the millisecond level — pauses, accelerations, and precise placements of hits/falls are critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performer skill: acrobat
rubrics_metrics.description: The slapstick comic must be: An acrobat
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical agility and body control enable safe, convincing pratfalls, flips, and movements. Assess physical conditioning and ability to execute acrobatic elements reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performer skill: stunt performer
rubrics_metrics.description: The slapstick comic must be: A stunt performer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stunt competence and safety awareness are required for risky physical gags. Proper technique and preparation reduce injury risk while maintaining comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performer skill: something of a magician
rubrics_metrics.description: The slapstick comic must be: Something of a magician
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misdirection and the ability to conceal mechanics (prop tricks, sleight-of-hand) help visual gags succeed. Evaluate how well the performer hides setup and reveals payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performer skill: master of uninhibited action and perfect timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The slapstick comic must be: Master of uninhibited action and perfect timing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full physical commitment (no flinching) and impeccable timing are essential; half-hearted execution ruins the gag. Assess commitment, facial/body neutrality during hits, and rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual Primacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty and hilarity come from visual nature — ideally, audience just watches and laughs without dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize clear visual storytelling over spoken explanation. Evaluate whether the gag reads purely visually and whether dialogue is unnecessary or distracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why it's funny (Bergsonian tie-in)
rubrics_metrics.description: Slapstick exemplifies 'the mechanical encrusted on the living' — a body that should be fluid and adaptive instead behaves like a rigid object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for a 'body-as-machine' quality: the comic effect often relies on making living bodies act mechanically or rigidly. Use this theory to shape poses, freezes, and mechanical movements for comedic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the action visually self-explanatory?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation question: the audience should understand the gag's setup and payoff just by watching. If viewers need verbal explanation, the visual clarity is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is timing precise (microseconds matter)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation question emphasizing micro-precision. Test and refine beats until the pause/impact durations reliably elicit the laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there anticipation/escalation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation question combining two structural elements: look for telegraphing that builds expectation and a sequence that escalates stakes/absurdity toward payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the performer fully committed (no flinching)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the performer fully committed (no flinching)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation question about performance commitment: half-commitment kills the gag. Check facial and bodily commitment through rehearsal and audience response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a body-as-machine element?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation question tied to Bergsonian theory: determine whether making the body behave mechanically (rigid, repetitive, object-like) is present and used for comic effect.
